rationale: B wins by doing the one thing A did not: it finds a real fourth protagonist without padding. "What it's actually like to rent your running shoes and mail them back to be ground up" gives a running/consumer desk a usable lane, while A leaves the same material buried as proof, "one named subscriber or pilot participant," then tells the founder to pick the category story. A is disciplined and mostly clean, but B gives the founder more choices and sharper stop-signs before anyone wastes a pitch.
gaps_in_A: "putting a core product behind" overstates the fact pattern; the update says Cyclon is a running shoe, not that it is core to On's product line.
"nationwide launch" never asks the country question; "nationwide" is useless for outlet targeting until you know which nation.
"one named subscriber or pilot participant" is treated as supporting proof, not as a standalone runner/customer angle, so A leaves an obvious consumer desk story on the floor.
"Next step: `meanest-editor` ... draft a tight pitch" is the wrong next move as written; fee, recycling rate, geography, and journalist fit come before copy.
gaps_in_B: "people who have already done a full cycle" is not in the update; a pilot existed, but completed run-return-replace cycles are still unproven.
"the reader can sign up now" assumes the reader is in the launch country; B later catches the geography problem, but the angle should not lean on it before it is answered.
"sneaker company" is a loose noun for a running/athletic brand; not fatal, but it is the kind of imprecision trade reporters notice.
